data.name: Chakrapani
data.gender_notes: Chakrapani is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Chakrapani is a Sanskrit name derived from the words ‘chakra’ meaning wheel and ‘pani’ meaning holder. This name signifies the deity Vishnu who holds the cosmic wheel, a symbol of power, protection, and the cycle of creation and destruction. The name Chakrapani carries the meaning “Holder of the wheel” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chakrapani usually hope their child will grow to embody holder of the wheel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes divine protection, power, and the cycle of creation and destruction.
data.etymology: Chakrapani belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Holder of the wheel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chakrapani total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Chakrapani is an evocative name in Hindu culture, conjuring images of strength, protection, and cosmic order. The name is synonymous with Lord Vishnu, a central deity in Hinduism and a preserver of the universe. Chakrapani is also a popular name among Vishnuite sects, particularly in India, where it is considered a significant and revered name.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Chakrapani holds deep spiritual significance. It symbolizes the power and protection bestowed by Lord Vishnu, who holds the cosmic wheel in his hands. The wheel, also known as the Sudarshana Chakra or the divine discus, represents the cycle of creation, preservation, and destruction in the universe. The name Chakrapani serves as a reminder of the divine protection and the cyclical nature of existence. It also encourages devotion and faith in Lord Vishnu, a deity revered for his unwavering presence and benevolence.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chakrapani, meaning 'Holder of the Wheel', symbolizes the divine power that steers the cycles of life and the universe, reminding us of the cosmic order and the cyclical nature of existence. Through this name, we are connected to the divine will and the cycle of time.
